verdicts.critique: This is the only proposal that attacks the actual binding constraint, and the framing defense is genuinely strong: DKKM PROVE complexity is worthless under exact factor pricing, so an APT economy is not a valid test bed, and saying so pre-empts the obvious 'you added mispricing' attack. But as written the paper dies on one sentence in the calibration section. The proposal sets kappa_med = SR_alpha_target * sigma_idio / (sqrt(N)*(1-rho)*M) = 0.6*0.10/(31.62*0.0378*1.5) = 0.033 -- i.e. the single economic parameter governing the new mechanism is solved backwards from a TARGET SHARPE, and that target is itself chosen to reproduce DKKM's published 2.6-3.4x ratio. The proposal even discloses the tension ('the binding constraint here is the reported SR*, not realism' -- 3.3% versus Rhodes-Kropf-Robinson-Viswanathan's 0.40 log sd). A JF referee reading that reverse-engineers the entire paper: you chose the wedge amplitude to hit the answer you wanted to report. Worse, kappa_med depends explicitly on N. That means max_sr is a function of the simulation's cross-sectional size, not of any equilibrium object -- the 'truth' the Sharpe metric scores against becomes a near-arbitrage whose Sharpe grows like sqrt(N) and that no agent inside the model exploits. Second problem, internal-consistency: sdf_compute currently computes ER from the model's own SDF and port = ER^{-1}1 is the mimicking portfolio for that SDF (verified, utils_bgn/sdf_compute_bgn.py:305-330; max_sr is the HJ bound). After the wedge, port is no longer any agent's SDF -- it is the statistical tangency portfolio of observed returns. The paper must say out loud that 'true SDF' has been redefined to 'unconstrained arbitrageur's frontier', and must explain why the arbitrageur who is being scored does not trade the wedge away. Third, technical: the wedge contaminates log bm ADDITIVELY (+q) and log size SUBTRACTIVELY (-q) by construction, so span{log bm_obs, log size_obs} = span{fundamentals} + 2q -- a LINEAR rule in two existing characteristics extracts most of the alpha. This puts the design in span2.py's 'linear alpha + heteroskedastic d' cell (RFF/lin = 1.91), not the 'nonlinear alpha' cell (6.37) the predicted-effect section leans on.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: Partly, and smaller than claimed. FM CAN reach the level of q linearly, for the reason above -- the observed chars are contaminated in opposite directions so a linear combination isolates the wedge. What FM cannot form is the modulation kappa(size,vol) x q / (d_f + kappa^2 sigma_v^2), which is the interaction. FF gets a two-bin approximation of the size half of that modulation through its 2x3 design (verified: fama_functions.py:83-104 builds one size x char double sort per characteristic), so FF is not shut out either. And note the FF factor as coded uses only the extreme buckets -- factor = 0.5*(high_big+high_small-low_big-low_small), the med portfolios are computed and discarded -- so it is a 2x2 monotone long-short and the hump argument does hold against FF. Net: I would expect a genuine but modest DKKM/FM span gap of roughly 1.5-2x, not 3-5x, unless s_k is pushed to ~1.9 to activate the hump -- at which point SR* is driven by the right tail of a lognormal arbitrage-cost distribution and the referee's N-scaling objection bites hardest. The gap is real but it is bought with the parameter that was reverse-engineered.
verdicts.salvage: Keep the wedge, kill the calibration. Three changes make this publishable. (1) GIVE THE DEMAND SHOCK AN AGGREGATE COMPONENT: v_it = w_t + e_it with w_t a common noise-trader factor carrying a price of risk. Then the wedge premium is DeLong-Shleifer-Summers-Waldmann compensation for noise-trader risk -- an equilibrium object, not a free lunch -- max_sr stops growing like sqrt(N), and the arbitrageur's failure to trade it away is modelled rather than assumed. This converts the referee's strongest attack into a citation. (2) CALIBRATE kappa TO AN EXTERNAL MOMENT AND FREEZE IT before running any estimator -- e.g. match the Rhodes-Kropf-Robinson-Viswanathan firm-specific misvaluation sd, or the observed magnitude of a standard anomaly long-short -- and report whatever SR* falls out, even if it is unflattering. State in the paper that the parameter was fixed ex ante. (3) REPORT THE N-SCALING TABLE: N in {250, 500, 1000, 2000} with kappa held FIXED. If DKKM/FF is stable in N the result is economics; if it scales with sqrt(N) it is diversification of a planted alpha and should be reported as such. Also, break the mechanical bm/size cancellation -- contaminate the price only, or add independent measurement noise -- so that recovering q genuinely requires the nonlinear basis rather than a two-char linear contrast.

verdicts.proposal_name: P2. Estimator geometry repair (bandwidth, second rank-standardization, NMAT, alpha grid, c=P/T)
verdicts.critique: Items (b)-(f) are correctness fixes I would insist on and they are cheap. I verified the diagnosis: dkkm_functions.py:110 does return rank_standardize(features) on the sin/cos block, and ridge_regr applies 1/(eigenvalues + 360*z) with no truncation at z=0 (lines 158-160 and 172-174), and mve_data always emits an unpenalized alpha=0 column first (line 301) with the market column exempted from the augmentation via np.eye(X.shape[1])[:-1] (line 311). ALPHA_LST = [0,0.001,0.01,0.05,0.1,1] with ALPHA_LST_GS = ALPHA_LST/100 is a hand-tuned per-model grid (config.py:190-193) and that alone is a referee finding: you gave one model a 100x-different regularization grid and did not say why. But item (a), the bandwidth rescale by sqrt(130/L), is where the paper gets killed. The derivation is elegant -- hold the Gaussian-kernel exponent gamma^2 L/12 fixed at DKKM's real-data value -- but the GS21 agent MEASURED that widening gamma HURTS when the truth is near-linear (36 features: 0.879 -> 0.799 at x4.65, 0.879 -> 0.376 at x10) and the theory agent measured it hurt in the estimation experiment too (0.157 vs 0.254 under linear alpha, homogeneous d). So the rescale is a knob whose sign depends on the DGP, and it will be adopted precisely because it helps under the new DGP. That is the definition of tuning, however good the derivation reads. The proposal's own risk section concedes 'do not apply it before P1/P3', which is an admission that the choice is conditioned on the answer. Bigger problem, item (f): the fairness fix is 'apply find_best_alpha_for_model to FF/FM as well'. I read that function (create_slides_tables.py:81-97): it takes the argmax over alphas of the MEAN Sharpe ACROSS iterations and then reports that alpha's per-iteration values -- post-hoc selection on the evaluation metric itself, with a SEPARATE argmin run for HJD, so two independent oracle choices per table cell. Letting FF/FM cheat symmetrically does not make the number out-of-sample; it institutionalizes the cheat and guarantees a referee comment. The correct fix is a validation split.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: No, and the proposal says so honestly -- on the current models the bundle is worth roughly zero because BGN's entire population nonlinearity headroom is 0.7pp of Sharpe and GS21's is 3%. That honesty is to its credit but it also means every point of gap this bundle eventually produces is attributable to estimator plumbing, and a referee will discount it to zero. There is a specific danger: the alpha-grid recentring plus c=36000 will make the DKKM column move visibly (the c=1 double-descent spike at P=T=360 disappears, alpha=0 stops realizing 1.4-13% of max Sharpe), and an incautious draft will read that movement as a result. It is a bug fix. Also NMAT: config.py:178 is NMAT=5 while the comment on the preceding line records that the root codebase used nmat=1 -- so the current setting is an undisclosed local deviation that provably flattens the complexity curve. Fixing it is mandatory, but fixing it will RAISE the Monte-Carlo variance of every DKKM cell and a single lucky draw must not become the headline.
verdicts.salvage: Split into two commits with different rhetorical status. COMMIT A (mandatory, pre-registered as bug fixes, report before/after on the CURRENT models so the reader sees they buy nothing): NMAT=5 -> 1 with the five draws reported as a distribution; the scale-free penalty reparameterization z*trace(X'X)/P, which also eliminates the indefensible GS21 /100; the 11-point log alpha grid; the same grid and the same tuning budget for FF/FM (fama_functions.mve_data:268 currently hardcodes Ridge(alpha=360*alpha) with ALPHA_LST_FAMA=[0]); turning on the commented-out FM standardization at fama_functions.py:152-156; and deleting the BGN-only rf_stand input at dkkm_functions.py:95-96, which is an unearned conditioning variable for DKKM that FF/FM never see and that the audit measured to be worth 89.9% vs 90.1% of max Sharpe, i.e. nothing. Drop it and lose nothing but a referee attack. COMMIT B (report as a robustness dimension, never as the baseline): the gamma rescale and the z-scoring of features, shown as a full 2x2 of {coded, rescaled} gamma x {old, new} DGP, so the reader can see the sign flip and judge it. AND replace symmetric oracle alpha selection with genuine out-of-sample hyperparameter selection: split the 360 eval months into a 120-month validation block used to pick (alpha, nfeatures) for every method and a 240-month test block used to report. That is the only version of this table I would let through.

verdicts.proposal_name: P3. Expand the characteristic set from 5-6 to ~35 model-generated signals
verdicts.critique: The proposal contains its own refutation and I would quote it back: DKKM's five-characteristic real-data experiment uses exactly this project's five characteristics and still delivers 0.74 -> 1.93-2.50. So the count is demonstrably not the cause, and adding thirty derived transforms of the same two or three latent states is dimension counting dressed as realism. The audit already measured the relevant placebo: at N=200 a basis of 150 RANDOM Gaussian directions carrying zero characteristic information attains 0.74-0.82 of max SR^2. If a random basis of the right size gets most of the way there, the referee's conclusion is that the gain is a property of the feature count, not of the information. Second, and more damaging: the proposal predicts on the current DGPs that 'FM Sharpe DOWN by roughly 10% from the 37-parameter estimation cost, FF Sharpe down more from 35 collinear sorted factors -- so this alone would produce a spurious-looking DKKM/FM ratio of maybe 1.2-1.3x that is pure estimation efficiency'. A gap produced by handicapping the benchmark is not a result; it is the thing referees are trained to look for. And the FF handicap is worse than stated, because FF's tercile logic degenerates whenever a characteristic has more than 30% ties -- I verified the code at fama_functions.py:86-88 uses data[char].quantile(0.3) and quantile(0.7) with no tie handling, which already breaks agr (91% zeros in BGN, 98.8% in GS21, giving q30 = q70 = 0 and an empty medium bucket). Several of the thirty new multi-horizon transforms in these near-static models will be similarly degenerate, and thirty degenerate sorts fed into an unpenalized OLS tangency at T=360 is not a benchmark, it is a straw man. Third, the fairness section is right that FF/FM must get the same 35 chars, but the proposal does not give FF ridge -- only P2(f) does, and if these ship separately the paper is indefensible.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: It would produce A gap, of the wrong kind. Effective rank rising 16.5 -> ~250 is real and the bandwidth by-product (sd(Wx) = gamma*sqrt(35/12) = 1.708*gamma with the ORIGINAL grid) is genuinely the referee-proof route to nonlinearity -- that part I like a lot, because it achieves P2(a) with no hyperparameter touched. But the mechanism producing the DKKM/FM ratio would be the 2K/T = 20.6% squared-Sharpe estimation penalty on a 37-parameter FM plus badly conditioned FF, and both of those are curable by the benchmark simply using ridge. The moment a referee asks 'what happens if FM is ridge-regularized on the same grid', the 1.2-1.3x collapses toward 1.0, because the truth is still low-dimensional and the extra chars are still redundant transforms of 2-3 states. FF is the only method that stays broken, and FF being bad at 35 collinear sorts is a known, uninteresting fact.
verdicts.salvage: Demote from a source of the result to an enabling change, and make three commitments. (1) Adopt it ONLY for the bandwidth by-product: state explicitly that raising L to ~35 is how the RFF index reaches genuine nonlinearity WITHOUT touching GAMMA_GRID, which removes P2(a)'s tuning exposure entirely. That is a real and defensible contribution. (2) Report ridge-regularized FM and ridge-regularized FF at the identical scale-free z-grid as the primary benchmarks, so that no part of the gap is estimation-cost handicapping. If DKKM still wins against a properly shrunk 37-characteristic linear model, the result is about nonlinearity and you can say so. (3) Screen every derived characteristic for tie fraction and drop anything above ~20% -- and fix the FF tercile degeneracy at fama_functions.py:86-88 in the same commit, because leaving it broken while adding thirty tie-heavy columns is the kind of thing that looks deliberate in hindsight. Also report the random-direction placebo (150 Gaussian directions) alongside the RFF column at every feature count; if RFF does not clearly beat the placebo, the dimension-counting objection is conceded.

verdicts.proposal_name: P4. Recalibrate the idiosyncratic-risk block in all three models
verdicts.critique: This is the only proposal that a referee cannot characterize as changing the model to get the answer, because it is undoing changes that were made to the models without disclosure. I verified BGN: panel_functions_bgn.py:54 reads high = np.abs(beta[:-1,:])/sigma_z + 0.1*0.3*np.abs(Cbar) with the inline comment '# added a factor of 0.1'. That is a 10x cut to the idiosyncratic cash-flow band, made in the repo, not in Berk-Green-Naik. KP14 has the same 10x cut on SIGMA_EPS and SIGMA_U, GS21 has 0.1*0.16 on SIGMA_Z. Here is the part the proposal understates and that the authors need to internalize: THE EXISTENCE OF THESE CUTS IS ITSELF A PAPER-KILLER IF A REFEREE FINDS THEM AND THE PAPER HAS NOT DISCLOSED THEM. A paper whose headline is 'these three canonical models cannot generate the virtue of complexity' while silently running all three at one tenth the source papers' idiosyncratic volatility -- producing average pairwise return correlations of 0.57, 0.39 and 0.95 against a real-data 0.15-0.20 -- is not recoverable at revision. So this must be done regardless of whether it helps, and the paper must contain a table of every parameter that differs from the source calibration with a reason for each. The proposal is also admirably honest that standalone this LOWERS max_sr everywhere and moves the DKKM/FF ratio by a few percent. My only real reservation is sequencing risk: GS21 needs a MATLAB re-solve on an external toolchain (the current solfiles' zgrid spans exactly +/-2.72 stationary sd of the 0.1x sigma_z, so at 0.5x everything extrapolates), and KP14 literally cannot be recalibrated until integ_results.npz and G_func.csv are fixed and kp14_fd.py's missing parameters_kp14 import is restored.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: On its own, no -- and the proposal says so, correctly. Under exact factor pricing the D^{-1} tilt is worth 0.186% of SR* at N=1000 even with a 20x spread in d, because idiosyncratic risk is diversifiable. FF could also get a crude version of the tilt if d is monotone in a single characteristic, which is exactly the KP14 case (corr(log idio var, log nlive) = -0.971). So as a standalone this changes nothing and would be correctly read as a null. Its value is as a multiplier: span2.py measures RFF/linear rising 1.00 -> 1.91 when heteroskedastic d is added to a linear alpha and 2.88 -> 6.37 when added to a nonlinear one. It also fixes two numbers that would otherwise draw fire on their own -- KP14's max_sr of 34.7 annualized against the model's own bound of 0.774, and GS21's 0.44/month of which 89-97% is diversifying 3.5-4.3 basis points of per-firm alpha across 500 near-identical firms. Neither of those is a Sharpe ratio anyone will believe.
verdicts.salvage: Adopt as written, with three additions. (1) A disclosure table in the paper listing every parameter that departs from the source paper's calibration, the departure, and the reason -- including the ones you revert, so the reader sees the history. (2) Fix KP14's numerics BEFORE any recalibration and before any KP14 number appears in any table: integ_kp14.py:43 calls quad(integrand, 0, 10, ...) against a CIR transition density with sd ~0.006 and silently returns exact zeros over the eps interval where 98% of firm-months live, which makes the KP14 'true' risk premium equal to minus the PVGO share -- wrong sign, dispersion 173x too large. Every KP14 row currently in the results is uninterpretable and must not be published in any form. (3) When you restore GS21's sigma_z, remove or guard the arbitrary floor at panel_functions_gs21.py:131 (P_ex = max(0.05/k, P_ex)) and add an eigenvalue check on cond_var before np.linalg.solve -- that clamp is the most plausible source of the 1e9 true SDF weights recorded in the original-vol run, and a silent near-singular solve is exactly the failure mode already documented in KP14.

verdicts.proposal_name: P5. Metric repair (scale-free pricing error, Sharpe/max_sr, unconditional Sharpe, better test assets)
verdicts.critique: Items (a)-(c) are mandatory and item (b) is the single most valuable line of code in this entire set. I confirmed it: calculate_moments.py:81-86 stores 'max_sr' in every moments dict, and evaluate_sdfs.py:170-179 reads m['rp'], m['cond_var'] and m['sdf_ret'] and never touches max_sr, so the ceiling never reaches a table. Since the reported Sharpe is exactly SR*_t x cos_Sigma(w, w*_t), a table of Sharpes without max_sr is uninterpretable -- neither the authors nor the referee can tell whether FF at 0.2423 is 20% or 81% of the ceiling, which is the entire difference between 'the estimator fails' and 'the model has nothing in it'. Publish that column and much of the paper writes itself. The HJD replacement is also correct algebra and GS21's reported FF HJD of 2.3465 alongside the best Fama Sharpe of 0.4433 is transparently a leverage artifact. BUT: changing the pricing-error metric between drafts, after the old one produced an inconvenient answer, is the second-most-likely thing a referee flags. Report both columns permanently and justify the new one from the derivation, never from the results. Now the item I would reject outright. P5(d) proposes adding test assets formed on 'ten deciles of the TRUE conditional MVE weight w*_t = solve(cond_var, rp)'. That is circular: you would build the test assets out of the answer key and then report that the method which best approximates the answer key prices them. Every method's alpha' Sigma^{-1} alpha against those portfolios is a monotone transform of cos_Sigma(w, w*) -- the Sharpe you already report -- dressed up as an independent pricing test. A referee will see it immediately and it will contaminate the credibility of the honest parts of the same table.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: No, by construction -- this changes no economics and the proposal says so. What it will do is make the existing null SHARPER and more publishable as a null: the Sigma-cosine column will show FF at roughly 0.81 and DKKM at 0.85 of the BGN ceiling, which demonstrates in one line that the estimators are near the ceiling and the DGP is the problem. That is a genuine contribution and arguably the paper's most persuasive exhibit whatever else happens. There is also a direction a referee should be told about: the scale-free pricing error REMOVES an asymmetry currently favoring DKKM, which gets six alphas selected post hoc on the evaluation metric (two separate oracle selections, one argmax for Sharpe and one argmin for HJD, at create_slides_tables.py:81-97) while FF/FM have alpha=0 only and no way to rescale. So the fix should make DKKM look slightly worse on pricing error. Disclose that, and disclose that it is the correct direction.
verdicts.salvage: Adopt (a), (b), (c) unchanged and make (b) a headline column in every table. Drop (d)'s w*-sorted decile portfolios entirely. Replace them with test assets that are informative but not circular: 5x5 on (mve, diag(cond_var)) is fine because idiosyncratic variance is a legitimate observable sort; add sorts on characteristic INTERACTIONS (size x bm, roe x agr) and on non-monotone transforms (|bm - median|, extreme deciles) -- these have power against nonlinear-in-characteristics mispricing without being built from the answer. Note the current 25 portfolios are mve x bm only (generate_25_portfolios.py:110-112, pd.qcut on the ranks of mve and bm), i.e. two of the five characteristics that all three methods already span linearly, so the existing test genuinely has no power and this is worth fixing. Also fix the universe mismatch in the same pass: evaluate_sdfs.py:170-171 subsets rp and cond_var to firm_ids from the estimator's panel while sdf_ret comes from moments computed over the book>0 universe, so the HJ benchmark and the method returns are not defined over the same assets.

verdicts.proposal_name: P6. Reporting lags with staggered fiscal year-ends plus heteroskedastic measurement error
verdicts.critique: The Fourier analysis is the best piece of theory in the whole set and I would want it in the paper regardless: classical homoskedastic errors-in-variables attenuates the linear component by lambda = tau^2/(tau^2+sigma_e^2) but attenuates frequency-omega components by exp(-omega^2 sigma_e^2/2), so it compresses the DKKM advantage exponentially while compressing FM's only classically. Deriving that, and then declining to add classical EIV because of it, is exactly the kind of reasoning that earns a referee's trust. The staleness half is also defensible -- staggered fiscal year-ends with a six-month lag is the Fama-French convention, not an invention, and it breaks GS21's genuinely indefensible identity bm = 1/P_ex exactly. But the heteroskedastic half is where I object. Setting sigma_e,i = sigma_e0*(mve_i/median)^{-xi} so that the optimal predictor becomes lambda_i x g(x_i) is writing a multiplicative interaction directly into the DGP and then reporting that the method with multiplicative features wins. That is the opposite of P1's virtue, where the ratio and the hump EMERGE from Sigma^{-1}mu rather than being written down. The sentence 'the authors introduced a variable whose only function is to multiply the other signals, and then found that a flexible estimator outperforms linear ones' is a rejection in one line. The proposal half-sees this -- it steers the reliability proxy toward staleness precisely because staleness is not one of FF's sort variables -- but that reasoning is itself incriminating: the proxy was chosen for being invisible to the benchmark rather than for being economically primary.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: Probably not against a competent benchmark, and this is the fatal technical objection. The truth is lambda(h_i) x bm_i, a product of an observable reliability variable with a signal. FM as coded regresses on chars linearly (fama_functions.fama_macbeth:159-165, X = [1, raw chars], P = X pinvh(X'X)), so naive FM cannot form it -- true. But nothing stops a referee from asking for FM run on {chars, h, chars x h}, which at L=5 is 16 regressors on 360 months, entirely feasible, and which spans the target to first order. If DKKM beats naive FM but not FM-with-interactions, there is no result, only a claim that the benchmark was specified badly. And FF is not shut out either: its 2x3 design already contains a size x char interaction, so if reliability had been left as a function of size FF would get a two-bin approximation -- which is why the proposal moved to staleness. The proposal also predicts honestly that the effect may be inert in BGN, where book = I*num is a small integer averaging 5.95 that barely moves month to month, so twelve-month-stale bm is nearly as informative as fresh. Finally, and this is a real self-inflicted wound: at P2's rescaled gamma the multiplicative noise costs a factor exp(-gamma^2 sigma_e^2/2) = 0.70 on exactly the nonlinear components the proposal exists to create.
verdicts.salvage: Keep the staleness mechanism, drop the heteroskedastic noise, and elevate the Fourier result to a standalone theoretical contribution. Specifically: (1) implement staggered fiscal year-ends and the six-month accounting lag as a pure realism layer with zero free parameters -- it is the standard convention, it breaks GS21's bm = 1/P_ex identity, and no referee can call it tuning; report the resulting DKKM/FM change honestly even if it is negative in BGN. (2) Do NOT add size-dependent measurement noise; the interaction is planted and the reliability proxy was visibly selected for being invisible to FF. (3) Publish the errors-in-variables asymmetry as a proposition with the exp(-omega^2 sigma_e^2/2) versus lambda contrast -- 'classical measurement error is a headwind for high-dimensional nonlinear SDF estimators and a tailwind for the case against them' is a genuinely novel and quotable point, and it makes the paper better even if the empirical exercise fails. (4) If any interaction-based mechanism survives, pre-commit to reporting FM with a full set of chars x reliability interactions and FF with the corresponding three-way sorts as primary benchmarks, not as robustness. The result must beat the benchmark a smart referee would build, not the one that happens to be in the repo.

missed_ideas: REPRODUCE THE REAL-DATA GAP WITH THIS EXACT PIPELINE FIRST. This is the check I would demand before reading any of the rest, and no proposal mentions it. Run generate_dkkm_factors / estimate_sdf_dkkm / estimate_sdf_fama unchanged on CRSP with the same five characteristics, T=360 rolling, and see whether the code reproduces DKKM's 0.74 -> 1.93-2.50. If it does not, every claim about what the MODELS lack is unfounded, because the estimator implementation is the confound -- and the audit gives specific reasons to worry (NMAT=5 is an undisclosed deviation from the root's nmat=1 at config.py:177-178; the second rank-standardization at dkkm_functions.py:110 makes GAMMA_GRID a near-no-op; the alpha grid has no point with effective df between 63 and 360). If it DOES reproduce the gap, that single exhibit converts the paper from 'we changed models until complexity paid' into 'our estimator is correct, and here is precisely what a structural model must contain for it to pay'. That reframing is worth more than any of the six proposals.

PUBLISH THE NEGATIVE CONTROL AS A HEADLINE EXHIBIT, NOT A FOOTNOTE. The single strongest defense against 'you tuned the DGP until it worked' is to show a DGP where you tuned nothing and it demonstrably does NOT work -- and you already have it in span2.py's exact-factor-pricing cell (SR* 0.0999, equal-weight 0.0998, linear span 0.0999, RFF 0.0994). Run the FULL pipeline, including the modified estimator, on the unmodified models and on a synthetic exact-APT panel, and report the flat complexity curve. A paper that shows the estimator failing where theory says it must fail, and succeeding only where theory says it can, is a paper about a mechanism. A paper that only shows the success is a paper about a search.

REPORT THE COMPLEXITY CURVE'S SHAPE, NOT ITS ARGMAX. DKKM's actual claim is about monotone ascent in c = P/T over three orders of magnitude, not about a single best cell. Yet create_slides_tables.py fixes nfeatures=3600 and then takes an argmax over alpha (line 100-101, two separate oracle selections for Sharpe and HJD). A monotone rising curve across c in {0.017, 0.1, 1, 10, 100} at a FIXED, pre-committed shrinkage is far harder to manufacture than a maximum over a grid, and it is the object the theory predicts. Make the curve the headline figure and relegate the argmax cell to an appendix.

MAKE THE PRICED-RISK SPACE HIGH-DIMENSIONAL INSTEAD OF ADDING A PRICING WEDGE. The diagnosis ranks 'raise the number of independently priced aggregate shocks from 1-2 to tens, with heterogeneous characteristic-dependent loadings' as the second binding blocker, and NO proposal implements it. This is the route a JF referee will fight least: it is fully rational, fully within the frictionless paradigm, requires no redefinition of 'the true SDF', keeps max_sr bounded independently of N, and is the direct lever on EffRank(E[FF']) -- DKKM's own Theorem 3 criterion, which needs hundreds and currently measures 16.5. Concretely: replace GS21's scalar x with a J-dimensional factor (sectoral, vintage, intangible-capital, financial-constraint shocks), give firms loading vectors that are nonlinear functions of their state, and price all J. It is more work than a three-line wedge, but P1's wedge buys a result the referee will discount by 80% while this buys one they cannot attack on identification grounds. At minimum it belongs in the paper as the alternative that was considered.

SELECT HYPERPARAMETERS OUT OF SAMPLE, DO NOT MAKE THE CHEATING SYMMETRIC. P2(f)'s proposal to let FF/FM also use find_best_alpha_for_model is the wrong repair. Split the 360 evaluation months into a validation block (say 120) used to pick (alpha, nfeatures) for every method and a disjoint test block (240) used to report. Every method then gets exactly one specification and one number, chosen without seeing the test data. This costs a third of the evaluation sample and removes the most predictable referee objection in the paper.

REPORT TURNOVER, GROSS LEVERAGE AND NET-OF-COST SHARPE. The audit already found the true HJ portfolio carrying 9x to 44x gross leverage in KP14, and GS21's max_sr is 89-97% driven by diversifying 3.5-4.3 basis points of alpha across 500 near-identical firms. If the manufactured DKKM advantage lives in extreme leverage on small, high-idiosyncratic-volatility names -- which is exactly where DKKM's real-data Sharpe of 3.7 lives, falling to ~1.6 in mega/large caps -- the paper should say so and report the advantage net of a plausible cost model. A referee who suspects the result is a microcap leverage artifact and finds no turnover table will assume the worst.

PRE-REGISTER THE PARAMETER CHOICES AND SHOW THE FULL SENSITIVITY SURFACE. P1's s_k is proposed as a search over {0.8, 1.3, 1.9} with the instruction 'pick the largest s_k for which SR* stays below ~2.5 annualized' -- i.e. pick the parameter that maximizes the mechanism subject to the answer staying plausible.
